extracted.intended_audience: general readers of literary fiction; writers interested in narrative technique and rhetoric
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and implied principles for composing or evaluating digressive, comic, eighteenth-century-style narrative voice — focusing on rhetorical devices, narrator persona, clarity, and aesthetic choices over strict factual exactness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer beauty over literal exactness
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an exact copying makes our pictures less striking, we choose the less evil; deeming it even more pardonable to trespass against truth, than beauty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a literal, exact account would make the presentation cold or vapid, alter or omit literal truth to preserve aesthetic or dramatic effect. The narrator explicitly defends sacrificing factual exactness for vividness or pleasure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interrupt or truncate narrative to preserve effect
rubrics_metrics.description: That the best plain narrative in the world, tacked very close to the last spirited apostrophe ... would have felt both cold and vapid upon the reader's palate;—therefore I forthwith put an end to the chapter, though I was in the middle of my story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: End or break the narrative at a moment that preserves emotional or rhetorical impact rather than continue with a plain, prosaic account that would lessen the effect. Chapter breaks and abrupt pauses are a deliberate stylistic tool.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sustain a consistent narrator persona
rubrics_metrics.description: You see as plain as can be, that I write as a man of erudition;—that even my similies, my allusions, my illustrations, my metaphors, are erudite,—and that I must sustain my character properly, and contrast it properly too,—else what would become of me?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain the narrator's voice and register (erudite, comic, pompous, etc.) consistently across devices — similes, allusions, metaphors — to preserve credibility of the speaker and comic effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity depends on perception, impression, and memory
rubrics_metrics.description: The cause of obscurity and confusion, in the mind of a man, is threefold. Dull organs ... Secondly, slight and transient impressions ... And thirdly, a memory like unto a sieve.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To produce clear discourse, attend to vivid perception (concrete sensory detail), strong and lasting impressions (salient description), and coherent memory/organization (structural signals); failures in any of these produce reader confusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid unsteady uses of words — prefer precise meanings
rubrics_metrics.description: What it did arise from ... and a fertile source of obscurity it is,—and ever will be,—and that is the unsteady uses of words, which have perplexed the clearest and most exalted understandings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose words with stable, determinate meanings; beware of logomachies and semantic slippage that generate scholarly disputes or ordinary confusion. Precision in terminology prevents needless argument and obscurity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Small rhetorical particles determine eloquence
rubrics_metrics.description: Just Heaven! how does the _Poco piu_ and the _Poco meno_ of the _Italian_ artists;—the insensible MORE OR LESS, determine the precise line of beauty in the sentence ... How do the slight touches of the chisel, the pencil, the pen, the fiddle-stick, et cætera,—give the true swell, which gives the true pleasure!
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attend to minor stylistic choices (dashes, pauses, small words, punctuation): tiny adjustments—aposiopesis, the dash, subtle rhythm—shape the sentence's beauty and the reader's pleasure. Don't dismiss small particles as insignificant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use rhetorical figures (aposiopesis, metaphor, omission) deliberately
rubrics_metrics.description: Make this dash,—’tis an Aposiopesis,—Take the dash away, and write 'Backside',—’tis Bawdy.—Scratch Backside out, and put 'Cover’d way' in, ’tis a Metaphor;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select rhetorical devices and strategic omissions consciously to modulate tone (e.g., to avoid bawdiness, to create decorum, to hint). These figures are tools for shaping what is said and what is suggested.

rubrics_metrics.name: Narrative time is elastic for effect
rubrics_metrics.description: If the hypercritick ... is resolved after all to take a pendulum, and measure the true distance betwixt the ringing of the bell, and the rap at the door ... I would remind him, that the idea of duration ... is got merely from the train and succession of our ideas ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compression and expansion of chronological time in narrative are permissible; the sequence and succession of ideas can determine perceived duration. Do not let pedantic temporal exactness constrain dramatic or rhetorical pacing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explain abstruse ideas with concrete, relatable examples
rubrics_metrics.description: Call down Dolly your chamber-maid, and I will give you my cap and bell along with it, if I make not this matter so plain that Dolly herself should understand it ... When Dolly has indited her epistle to Robin ... take that opportunity to recollect that the organs and faculties of perception can ... be aptly typified ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To instruct or clarify abstract points, use vivid, everyday analogies and scenes accessible to a lay reader. Concrete illustration (Dolly's thimble and wax) makes complex points intelligible and comic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Court and include critics rather than exclude them
rubrics_metrics.description: There is nothing so foolish, when you are at the expence of making an entertainment of this kind, as to order things so badly, as to let your criticks and gentry of refined taste run it down: Nor is there any thing so likely to make them do it, as that of leaving them out of the party ... I have left half a dozen places purposely open for them;—and in the next place, I pay them all court.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As a social/strategic rule for presenting work, do not alienate critics by excluding or ignoring them; include and attend to critics' sensibilities to reduce hostile reception. (This mixes social strategy with presentation of one's work.)
